provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Back to discovery
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what science is.
The pupils should be able to list discovery corner rules.
Introduction:
We love to learn new things. Science helps us discover.
Content:
Science is asking why. Why is the sky blue? Why do plants grow? Discovery corner rules are simple. Be gentle with objects. Share with friends. Wash hands after touching.
Class activity:
Let's sing a discovery song. Point to things in the classroom and ask why.
Evaluation questions:
What is science? Name one discovery rule. What do we do after touching objects?
Summary:
Science is asking why. We follow rules in our discovery corner.

topics.title: My body inside
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to point to their heart.
The pupils should be able to explain what lungs do.
Introduction:
We have special parts inside us. We learned about body parts last term.
Content:
The heart is a special muscle. It pumps blood all around your body. You can feel your heartbeat after running. Lungs help you breathe. They fill with air when you inhale.
Class activity:
Let's run in place for one minute. Then place hands on chest to feel heartbeat.
Evaluation questions:
Where is your heart? What do lungs do? How does your heart feel after running?
Summary:
Your heart pumps blood. Your lungs help you breathe.

topics.title: Teeth types
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify front teeth and back teeth.
The pupils should be able to count their own teeth.
Introduction:
We use teeth to eat food. Different teeth do different jobs.
Content:
Front teeth are called incisors. They bite food like apples. Back teeth are called molars. They chew food like yam. Adults have more teeth than babies.
Class activity:
Let's count our teeth together. Open mouth wide and point to front teeth.
Evaluation questions:
What are front teeth called? What are back teeth called? How many teeth do you have?
Summary:
Front teeth bite. Back teeth chew.

topics.title: Animals around school
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name three animals.
The pupils should be able to spot animals around school.
Introduction:
Animals live everywhere. We see some at school and home.
Content:
Birds can fly. Lizards have tails. Insects have six legs. Some animals live in trees. Some live in grass. We must be quiet when watching animals.
Class activity:
Let's walk quietly around school. We will look for animals and name them.
Evaluation questions:
Name three animals. How many legs do insects have? Where do birds live?
Summary:
Animals live all around us. We must be quiet when watching them.

topics.title: Animal coverings
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name fur, feathers and scales.
The pupils should be able to sort animals by their coverings.
Introduction:
Animals have different coverings. Some are soft. Some are hard.
Content:
Animals with fur are soft like cats. Animals with feathers can fly like birds. Animals with scales have hard skin like fish. Coverings protect animals from harmattan heat.
Class activity:
Let's sort animal cards. Put all furry animals together. Put all scaly animals together.
Evaluation questions:
Name one animal with fur. What animal has feathers? What covers a fish?
Summary:
Animals have fur, feathers or scales. Coverings protect them.

topics.title: How animals move
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name four ways animals move.
The pupils should be able to act like different animals.
Introduction:
Animals move in different ways. Some fast. Some slow.
Content:
Animals walk on legs like dogs. Animals fly with wings like birds. Animals swim with fins like fish. Animals crawl on their belly like snakes. Movement helps animals find food.
Class activity:
Let's play animal movement game. I will call an animal and you move like it.
Evaluation questions:
How do birds move? How do fish move? How do snakes move?
Summary:
Animals walk, fly, swim or crawl. Movement helps them live.

topics.title: Plants in our compound
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name three types of plants.
The pupils should be able to do bark rubbing art.
Introduction:
Plants grow around us. They are important for life.
Content:
Trees are tall plants with strong trunks. Grass covers the ground. Flowers are colorful plants. Plants give us shade. They clean the air we breathe.
Class activity:
Let's make bark rubbing. Place paper on tree bark and rub with crayon.
Evaluation questions:
Name three types of plants. What do plants give us? How do we make bark rubbing?
Summary:
We have trees, grass and flowers. Plants are good for us.

topics.title: Seeds
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to collect different seeds.
The pupils should be able to sort seeds by size.
Introduction:
Seeds grow into plants. We eat some seeds.
Content:
Seeds come in different sizes. Some are small like groundnut. Some are big like mango seed. All seeds have a baby plant inside. Seeds need water to grow.
Class activity:
Let's collect seeds from different fruits. We will sort them into big and small.
Evaluation questions:
What is inside a seed? Do all seeds look the same? What do seeds need to grow?
Summary:
Seeds grow into plants. They come in different sizes.

topics.title: Water everywhere
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name three sources of water.
The pupils should be able to explain how we use water.
Introduction:\ Water is all around us. We need water every day.
Content:
Rain falls from the sky. Tap water comes from pipes. River water flows in nature. We drink water to live. We use water to cook jollof rice. We use water to wash our hands.
Class activity:
Let's sing about water. Name all the ways we use water at home.
Evaluation questions:
Where does rain come from? Name two ways we use water. Why do we need water?
Summary:
Water comes from rain, tap and river. We use water every day.

topics.title: Revision and discovery walk
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to show something they found.
The pupils should be able to tell about their find.
Introduction:
We learned many things this term. Let's go find more.
Content:
Nature is full of discoveries. We can find leaves, stones, seeds and insects. We must be careful with living things. We can take pictures but not hurt plants.
Class activity:
Let's go on a discovery walk. Collect interesting things to show the class.
Evaluation questions:
What did you find? Why should we be careful with nature? What did you learn this term?
Summary:
Nature has many things to discover. We must respect all living things.
